editions.text:
Yesterday brought a notable drop in species count, with only 14 recorded compared to the previous week’s average of 20. Feeder traffic remained high at 311 visits, well above the weekly average of 199, driven largely by the regulars who held their spots every single day: Carolina Wren, Northern Cardinal, Eastern Towhee, Carolina Chickadee, House Finch, and Tufted Titmouse.

Several species present in the prior seven days were missing, including Northern Mockingbird, Red-shouldered Hawk, and Pileated Woodpecker. A single Common Raven was detected in the 22:00 hour, a species not recorded in the immediate prior days but seen earlier in the week.
